newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia Jan-Aug foreign investment falls.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia Jan-Aug foreign investment falls.

text.p: Indonesia's Investment Minister Sanyoto Sastrowardoyo said on Monday foreign investment approvals during January 1 to August 31 fell to $22.2 billion from $29.7 billion in the same period last year.
He told reporters that the falls were due to a lack of major projects.
"But in terms of total projects, there was an increase. During the January-August period, the total increased to 677 projects compared to 508 projects in the same period last year," Sanyoto added.
Sanyoto said he believed this showed foreign investor interest in Indonesia remained high, but he added he was not optimistic that foreign investment approvals in 1996 would match the 1995 figure.
Indonesia posted record foreign investment approvals of $39.9 billion last year.
"We expect foreign investment will increase steadily in the coming years after government regulations allowing tax holidays," he said.

But he gave no details on the proposed moves for granting tax holidays. Indonesia has said it will give tax breaks to newly established companies in certain sectors but has not revealed which industries would benefit.
